title: VF-023's second probe: which ingredient of the corpus's listSizes and listChange makes JBMC refute a one-element list's size
description: Values stream of llm-dlc/loops/application-core.md (llm-dlc/loops/application-core-values.md, acceptance row V2; finding VF-023 in verification/findings.md), at the commit that submits this job. Job 20261108-070211-… failed at step 2 because under --engine auto --confirm JBMC 6.11.0 refutes the conformance corpus's listSizes [assume n >= 1 && n <= 3; assert result == n * 10] with n=1 and listChange [assume n == 0 || n == 8; assert result == 1] with n=0, which the own checker proves and the JVM and the interpreter hold. The first probe (job 20261108-082244-…, passed) refuted the guess that class initialization order is the cause: JBMC proves List.of(new Object()).size() == 1 alone, after List.of(), and a two-element list's size 2. This job changes nothing. verification/triage/vf023-choice.sh runs nine property proofs with JBMC alone (jvmcontract prove --engine jbmc, the default unwind 16, timeout 300 s each, lib/models on JBMC's class path as always), one ingredient at a time: the corpus's own two methods (compiled from lib/tests/conformance/conformance/Conformance.java), then a choice between two List12s (oneOrTwo), between a List12 and a ListN (oneOrThree), between EMPTY_LIST and a List12 (emptyOrOne), a one-element list under listSizes' assumption (oneAssumed), with three objects made first (oneMadeFirst), listChange's choice of list without its switch (changeNoSwitch), and its switch over a one-element list without the choice (oneThenSwitch). From each refutation it keeps JBMC's failed property, its description, and the trace steps that assign a list's fields, ImmutableCollections' statics, a class identifier or an initialization flag, with the last 40 steps. Domain: one int n under each probe's assumption. Expected verdicts: corpusSizes and corpusChange refuted by JBMC with a witness the interpreter doesn't reproduce, so jvmcontract says the violation isn't reproduced (VF-023 reproduced); the seven others unknown, which is the question. On a JVM every claim holds (printed first, and checked inline), and the own checker proves all nine (checked inline). Expected process status: the script exits 0 (1 only if a probe fails to compile); matchesExpected is the script running to the end. The verdicts and traces in lib/target/vf023-choice/summary.txt are the evidence.
expected: exits 0, with summary.txt naming each of the nine probes' verdicts, and for each refutation JBMC's failed property and trace steps

resources.notes: nine JBMC runs over methods of a few lines: the first probe's three took 0.2 s each, the corpus's list claims under 10 s each under JBMC
